120	Now, after we have seen the Torah and the verse
121	in the Writings, in the book of Kohelet, let's look at the Mishnah
122	in tractate Bava
123	Metzia, chapter 4 of Bava Metzia, it is written as follows:
124	If he drew the fruit but did not give him the money, he cannot
125	retract. If he gave him the money but did not draw the fruit,
126	he can retract. But they said: He who punished the people of the generation
127	of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion
128	will exact payment from one who does not stand by his word. Let's try to understand this.
129	First of all, let's study only the topic there in tractate Bava
130	Metzia.
131	Tractate Bava Metzia is the middle tractate between
132	two other tractates, Bava Kamma and Bava Batra. These three
133	tractates, Bava Kamma, Bava Metzia and Bava Batra,
134	make up a larger tractate called Nezikin,
135	which actually deals with, and it is found in the order
136	of Nezikin, one of the six orders of the Mishnah in the Talmud.
137	And these tractates deal with matters
138	of monetary law. In chapter 4 of Bava Metzia, it speaks about
139	the system of acquisitions, how one acquires things. That is, there are
140	objects that are mine, property that is mine,
141	and the question is how an asset becomes mine or
142	leaves my possession. Now, here we are talking about two
143	people in the discussion here
144	in the Mishnah,
145	where one sells fruit to another,
146	say a greengrocer or a fruit seller
147	in the market, the fruits are of course not his, and now
148	a buyer comes and wants to buy. So one must know that
149	when buying fruit, the acquisition is not made by payment of
150	money, as is commonly thought today, but rather
151	the acquisition is made by means of
152	drawing, meaning from the moment the buyer drew the thing
153	that he is buying, in this case fruit, a kind, from
154	his domain, drew it, that is, he joined it to himself,
155	that is what creates the acquisition, even if he has not yet
156	paid
157	the money. Let me give an example. Imagine a person
158	walks into a shop, not one that sells fruit and vegetables,
159	but he goes to buy a vase or some
160	glass item, right? So there is the display
161	in the shop, and he says to the seller: I want the
162	third vase there on the second shelf from the
163	right. The seller goes and takes down
164	this one,
165	and this vase falls
166	and breaks. Even if he paid the
167	money, the customer, as it were, only needs to be brought
168	this one. The payment of money does not make the acquisition until
169	the vase actually reaches his possession. That is, what
170	makes the acquisition here is
171	the drawing. Now, after more or less this principle,
172	let's look again at the Mishnah: If he drew the
173	fruit and did not give him
174	the money. They agreed that he buys from him, I don't know how many,
175	ten crates of oranges or apples, I don't know
176	what. The customer drew the fruit from the shop
177	owner and still did not give him the fruit, did not give
178	him the money, he has not yet paid him, he only
179	drew and did not pay the money, and afterwards he wants
180	to retract. He says: You know what, no, I don't
181	want the fruit, it is not good, I am not buying it. But he already drew it. The shop owner can say
182	to him:
183	Sorry, you drew it, it is already yours, I am not willing to take
184	it back. This is the meaning of: He drew fruit from him and did not
185	give him money, he cannot retract. If he gave him
186	money and did not draw fruit from him, that is, they
187	agreed that he buys these crates of oranges
188	and he already paid him the money but still did not
189	draw it, he can retract,
190	because there was no acquisition here. What is the determining acquisition?
191	It is the acquisition of drawing. Now, what happens here? The Mishnah
192	addresses this and says: But they said: He who punished
193	the people of the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion will
194	exact payment from one who does not stand by his word. That is,
195	you committed yourself, true, you have not yet carried out the acquisition, but
196	you committed yourself. So by strict law you may retract.
197	But know that this is a grave matter, what is written here: He who
198	punished the people of the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion
199	will exact payment from one who does not stand by his word. The generation
200	of the Flood is the story that appears at the end of the book, at the end
201	of Parashat Bereshit, the beginning of Parashat Noach, right: All flesh corrupted
202	its way upon the earth, and I am destroying them with the earth,
203	and the Flood came
204	and actually destroyed all
205	living things. The people of the generation of the Flood were wicked people,
206	and the Holy One, blessed be He, destroyed them. Ten generations
207	later they built the Tower of Babel, this is the generation of the Dispersion, in which
208	at first the whole earth was of one language and one speech,
209	and then the Holy One, blessed be He, confused their language, and this is called
210	Dispersion, He divided
211	them. And this punishment of the generation of the Flood and of the generation
212	of the Dispersion is the punishment of a person who does not stand
213	by his word. And here note that the Mishnah is not speaking about
214	matters between man and God, it is speaking about matters between
215	man and his fellow, about a commercial
216	commitment, by word, by word. So it is true that apparently
217	there was no drawing here, and therefore you cannot, the shop
218	owner cannot say to him: Listen, you drew it, it is yours.
219	He can retract, but if he retracts,
220	he is in fact breaking his word, breaking his promise.
221	One who breaks his promise, it is written here something very
222	severe, that he is destined to end like the people of the generation of the
223	Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion ended, and one must know that these matters
224	are not trivial. One must understand what happened
225	in the generation of the Flood and in the generation of the Dispersion that is connected to the matter of
226	not standing
227	by one's word. What all this shows us is that speech is
228	a very, very
229	serious thing. We came out of this, remember this whole journey,
230	we started from the verses in the Torah, the three verses in the Torah
231	in the book of Devarim in our parashah, Parashat Ki Tetze: When
232	you vow a vow to HaShem, do not delay to pay it, and so on.
233	We saw the verses also in Kohelet, we saw now
234	this Mishnah in Bava Metzia, and now let's
235	try to go a bit deeper. Perhaps we will start with the matter
236	of what the connection is between standing by one's word and the terrible punishment
237	that appears here, which is compared to the generation of
238	the Flood and the generation of
239	the Dispersion. So for this purpose, let's go to the book of Bereshit.
